props.title: Our Hospitality
props.initialSlug: City slicker stumbles into deadly family feud

sections.content: Buster Keaton's Our Hospitality (1923) marks a pivotal evolution in silent comedy, expanding beyond pure slapstick into narrative sophistication. The film cleverly satirizes the Hatfield-McCoy feud while showcasing Keaton's remarkable physical comedy and innovative filmmaking. It follows his earlier work The Three Ages (1923), but demonstrates far more ambition in both scope and storytelling. Keaton's commitment to practical effects reaches new heights here - the waterfall rescue sequence remains one of silent cinema's most dangerous stunts, performed without tricks or doubles.

sections.content: The film's historical setting proved hugely influential on period comedies that followed. Three Ages (1923) had dabbled in historical segments, but Our Hospitality committed fully to meticulous 1830s period detail, from authentic locomotives to period-accurate clothing. This attention to historical accuracy while maintaining comedy's pace would influence works like The General (1926) and even modern films like Shanghai Noon (2000).

The technical innovations in Our Hospitality were groundbreaking for their time. Keaton's use of practical effects, especially in the river rescue sequences, established new possibilities for action-comedy. His work here directly influenced later silent masterpieces like Harold Lloyd's Safety Last! (1923) and Charlie Chaplin's The Gold Rush (1925), particularly in their blend of death-defying stunts with character-driven comedy. SUBHEAD: Impact on Comedy Filmmaking

sections.content: The film's influence extends far beyond its era. Its fish-out-of-water premise and culture clash comedy can be traced through films like Some Like It Hot (1959) and Trading Places (1983). The combination of action setpieces with comedy DNA appears in everything from Jackie Chan's Project A (1983) to Back to the Future Part III (1990), which similarly uses period trains as both historical detail and action setting.
